role_in_set: Umbrella/summary subject closing the organelles set: the generic textbook animal cell, showing the parts already rendered individually in this atlas (nucleus, ER, Golgi, mitochondrion, lysosome, ribosome, cell membrane, cytoskeleton) assembled into one working whole. It is deliberately NOT one particular cell type - it is the floor plan every body cell in the later sets varies.

morphology.summary: A generic eukaryotic animal cell: an irregular, rounded (never perfectly spherical) mass of cytoplasm bounded ONLY by its plasma membrane - no wall of any kind. Typical human cells run about 10-30 um across (the atlas's generic figure: ~20 um). Inside the cytoplasm sit the membrane organelles: ONE nucleus (double-membrane envelope with pores, containing chromatin and one prominent nucleolus), rough ER as connected, ribosome-studded cisternae continuous with the outer nuclear membrane, smooth ER as a tubular network without ribosomes, ONE Golgi apparatus as a SEPARATE polarised stack of flattened cisternae with budding vesicles, SEVERAL mitochondria (each with smooth outer membrane and inner membrane folded into cristae), a few lysosomes (single membrane, granular interior), free ribosomes as thousands of tiny dots through the cytosol, one centriole pair (two short barrels at right angles, near the nucleus), and cytoskeleton filaments threading the cytoplasm. The honest classic teaching view is a CUTAWAY/SECTIONED cell so the interior shows.
morphology.kind: generic eukaryotic cell (the shared blueprint of all animal body cells); an umbrella subject, not a species
morphology.size: Most human body cells are 10-30 um across; ~20 um is the usual generic figure. For orientation inside it: nucleus ~6 um, mitochondria 0.5-1 um wide and 1-4 um long (usually the largest count of any organelle, hundreds to thousands per real cell - a teaching cutaway shows several), lysosomes 0.1-1 um, ribosomes ~25-30 nm (drawn as dots), plasma membrane ~5-10 nm thick (drawn as a single thin line at this scale), centrioles ~0.2 x 0.4 um.
morphology.shape: Irregularly rounded - a soft, gently lumpy blob whose outline is set by the cytoskeleton and by neighbours, NOT a perfect sphere and NOT a box. Because only a flexible membrane bounds it, real animal cells are asymmetric and slightly amoeboid in outline. The teaching convention is a rounded cell drawn in cutaway (a wedge or half removed) so the organelles inside are visible in place.
morphology.number_per_cell: One nucleus with one prominent nucleolus; one Golgi stack (teaching convention; real cells can have several); several mitochondria in view (standing for hundreds); a handful of lysosomes; one centriole pair; thousands of ribosomes (drawn as many small dots, both free and studding the rough ER).
morphology.arrangement: The nucleus sits roughly central. Rough ER wraps around and is CONTINUOUS with the outer nuclear membrane; smooth ER continues from the rough ER further out. The Golgi stack sits near the nucleus but SEPARATE from the ER - a distinct pile of flattened sacs with small transport vesicles between ER and Golgi and budding from the Golgi rims. Mitochondria and lysosomes scatter through the cytoplasm. The centriole pair sits near the nucleus. Cytoskeletal filaments radiate through the cytosol to the membrane.

distinguishing_conventions.golgi_vs_er: Golgi = a SEPARATE stack of smooth flattened discs (no ribosome dots) with vesicles budding at the rims; rough ER = CONNECTED, continuous folded cisternae studded with dots, flowing out of the nuclear envelope. The two must not merge into one membrane mass.
distinguishing_conventions.mitochondrion: Double membrane: smooth outer line, inner membrane folded inward as wide wavy ribbons (cristae) like a rippled curtain. Never a plain empty capsule.
distinguishing_conventions.lysosome_vs_mitochondrion: Lysosome = ONE membrane line, round, granular/speckled interior, no folds. Mitochondrion = TWO membranes with cristae.
distinguishing_conventions.nucleus: Double envelope (two close parallel lines) with pore interruptions, dense heterochromatin patches at the rim, one darker rounded nucleolus with no membrane of its own.
distinguishing_conventions.smooth_vs_rough_er: Same membrane colour; rough ER carries dots and sits near the nucleus, smooth ER is a dot-free tubular network continuing outward.

do_not_draw: No rigid cell wall - the outline is a single soft membrane line (a wall is the plant cell's/bacterium's).
No chloroplasts - those belong to the plant cell subject.
No large central vacuole - that is the plant cell's water tank; animal cells have at most small vesicles.
No perfectly spherical, geometric outline - the cell is irregularly rounded.

No baked-in text of ANY kind. This subject is the single most label-contaminated diagram in every textbook training set: every printed version carries lettered callouts. All surfaces must be clean, unlettered biological material; verification must check magnified crops of every region for lettering.
No metaphase chromosomes (X shapes) inside the intact nucleus.
No bacterial structures (flagellum, pili, nucleoid, capsule).
No anthropomorphising in the scientific plates (faces belong only on the colouring page).

colour_legend: All colour is teaching convention (cells are colourless; TEM is greyscale). Kept consistent with the sibling plates of this set: cell body warm translucent cream/tan; plasma membrane thin steel-blue/teal line; nuclear envelope two blues (outer #6B8CB8, inner #4C6E9E) with amber (#F2B441) pore rings; heterochromatin dusty purple (#7B4B8A), euchromatin lavender (#C9A6D6); nucleolus terracotta (#D9622B); rough + smooth ER cool grey-blue (#9AA7B5) with dark ribosome dots only on the rough part; Golgi dusty sage-green (#8FAE8B) stack; mitochondria steel-blue outer membrane with warm dusty-rose (#C98A7A) interior and pale cristae ribbons; lysosomes muted mauve (#A07B9E) with speckles; ribosomes tiny dark slate dots; centrioles small amber-grey barrels; cytoskeleton fine pale threads.
